brief: ORRERY SYNTH: a generative music instrument built as a working orrery (a clockwork solar-system model). Drag outward from the sun to launch a planet; release sets its orbit radius. Orbital period follows Kepler's third law (T proportional to a^1.5), so outer planets move slower. Every planet sounds a note each time it crosses the meridian (a fixed hairline at 12 o'clock), so the whole system becomes a self-playing polyrhythm. Radius maps to pitch on the current scale (inner = high, outer = low), quantized to concentric staff rings drawn like an engraved brass orrery. Must include: Web Audio voices with a soft envelope (FM or additive bell/marimba timbre); a generated convolution reverb (noise-burst impulse response); a tempo-synced feedback delay; a master DynamicsCompressor limiter so dense systems never clip; a scale picker (major pentatonic, minor pentatonic, Dorian, Lydian, Hirajoshi, whole-tone) with correct interval sets; a root-note selector; a tempo (time scale) control; select a planet by tapping it, remove with Delete/Backspace or a Remove button, plus Clear; moons: drag from a planet to give it a moon that orbits it and plays an octave up when it crosses the planet's own meridian; a pulse ring and a brief meridian glow each time a note fires; faint orbit trails. A 'Sound on' button is required before audio (autoplay is blocked); visuals run immediately with a pre-seeded 5-planet system so the first frame is alive. Live readouts in the subject's terms: orbital period in beats, note name (e.g. D4), radius. Keyboard: Space pauses, number keys switch scale. Audio must be crackle-free: schedule notes ahead with AudioContext.currentTime lookahead instead of firing straight from rAF timing, and cap polyphony.
